subject: Latency & context-window pulse check — qualification + next steps
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Barnes <alex@veridian.health>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Latency & context-window pulse check — qualification + next steps

Alex — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick written recap so we have alignment on the performance/SLO items we discussed and clear next steps.

Summary of what you asked us to qualify:
- Latency targets: p50 ~100–150ms, p95 target 250–350ms for user-facing typed responses.
- Throughput/concurrency: steady 200 RPS for peak clinic hours, 500 RPS burst during check-in spikes.
- Streaming: partial/transcript streaming required for live note-taking flows (low-latency partial output is critical).
- Context window: typical prompts ~3–5k tokens, but archival-transcript cases up to ~16k input tokens with ~1–2k output.

Immediate perf implications we flagged on the call:
- Large context (8k–16k) increases per-token model compute and KV-cache pressure; expect p95 to increase nonlinearly with sequence length.
- Streaming lowers perceived latency for users but can increase aggregate compute (more frequent shorter responses) and may affect throughput at the same GPU concurrency.
- Fallbacks: model-variant rollbacks or truncated-prefix fallbacks reduce latency but need application-level acceptability checks.

Attachments: I attached a short Redwood SLO playbook draft with our recommended target bands and a recording of today’s demo.

Immediate asks for you (so we can run a representative perf qualification):
1) Share a 24–72 hour sample of request payloads (prompt lengths, typical vs worst-case) — the CSV you mentioned is perfect.
2) Confirm whether streaming must deliver partial tokens as they’re generated, or if batched partials (250–500ms) are acceptable.
3) Any regulatory constraints that require on-prem/private deployment for PII paths? (helps us recommend Dedicated vs Hosted routing).

Proposed next steps (we can adjust after we see the load: )
- Engineering sync (30–45m): propose Wed 21 Jul, 10am PT — Rishi will join to scope perf lab.
- Redwood will run an initial perf pass against a 16k/4k mixed workload (your CSV) and share preliminary p50/p95 numbers and a recommended canary config.
- If streaming is required, we’ll propose a chunking strategy and an estimated p95 delta for long-context transcripts.

Thanks — I’ll tee up the meeting and include a short checklist for the perf run.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
(Attachment: redwood_slo_playbook_draft.pdf, demo-recording-20270718.mp4)

From: Alex Barnes <alex@veridian.health>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency & context-window pulse check — qualification + next steps

Lauren — really helpful summary, thanks. A few clarifications and I attached the sample you asked for (veridian_load_profile.csv).

Answers:
- Streaming: for live notes we need token-by-token streaming to the UI for best UX. We can accept small batching for analytics jobs but not for clinician-facing live flows.
- Payloads: typical interaction is 3–5k tokens, but ~1% of sessions are transcript-heavy (12–16k). The attached CSV has token counts and an anonymized distribution.
- Regulatory: PHI is in scope; we prefer Dedicated or VPC-private routing for any production PHI paths, but we’re open to a hybrid approach for non-PHI.

Question on fallbacks: if we detect a 16k input is causing p95 spikes beyond your SLA, what are the recommended graceful-degradation strategies? We discussed model variant fallbacks on the call — can you outline the tradeoffs (latency vs quality) briefly?

Thanks — I’ll be on the engineering sync if you set it up.

—Alex
Alex Barnes
Head of Product Engineering | Veridian Health
(Attachment: veridian_load_profile.csv)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency & context-window pulse check — qualification + next steps

Alex — great, thanks for the CSV and the clarifications. Summary of what Redwood will do and what we need from Veridian to complete the qualification: 

Redwood action items (ownership in parens):
1) Run perf lab (Redwood infra) against the attached veridian_load_profile.csv including: 3k/5k typical mix and a 12–16k tail. We’ll measure p50/p95, throughput backpressure, and memory/KV-cache behavior (Rishi).
2) Streaming experiment: evaluate token-by-token streaming vs 250ms micro-batch mode using a transcript-shaped workload. We’ll produce user-visible latency numbers and delta vs non-streaming (Monica).
3) Canary recommendation: after perf pass, propose a canary config (10% traffic, auto-fallback to a 4k-variant model for detected heavy inputs, route PHI through Dedicated) and an estimate of expected p95 delta under sustained bursts (Lauren).

Veridian asks we need answered (action / deadline):
- Confirm PHI path gating: which endpoints must be routed to Dedicated? (Action: Alex; deadline: Wed 21 Jul end of day)
- Confirm whether token-by-token streaming is mandatory or if 150–300ms micro-batches are tolerable for the worst-case transcripts (Action: Alex; deadline: Tue 20 Jul EOD)
- Share any additional load shapes (long-tail weekend vs weekday) if available (Action: Alex; deadline: Fri 23 Jul).

Notes on tradeoffs (short):
- 16k inputs: we can support via chunked prefixing + KV cache stitching, but expect p95 to increase ~30–80ms depending on model variant and GPU type. Quantized variants reduce latency but can reduce answer fidelity on medically nuanced prompts.
- Streaming: token-by-token gives best UX but increases throughput by ~10–25% because of smaller microrequests; micro-batching (200–300ms) can often hit a good point for perceived latency vs cost.

Next meeting: I scheduled the engineering sync for Wed 21 Jul, 10am PT. Rishi and Monica will run the perf scenarios immediately after and share a preliminary readout by Thu 22 Jul EOD.

If that plan looks good, I’ll upload the perf checklist and the lab-test plan to the Drive link and open a HubSpot activity (VER-4312).

Thanks — looking forward to making steady progress.

—Lauren
